title: Markets as Exchange Mechanisms
statements: Voluntary exchange in a market occurs when both parties expect to gain from the trade.
A market requires face-to-face bargaining and excludes nationwide online listings.
A market exists only where a government agency sets every transaction price.
Prices in a market serve only as receipts and carry no information about scarcity.
Repair workshops cannot form a market because their output is intangible advice.

title: Vienna Naschmarkt Stallholders
statements: Weekend crowds willing to pay more can raise equilibrium price for fresh herbs at the stall.
A wholesale cost increase may reduce quantity supplied at each price unless the stall raises its selling price.
A price above equilibrium clears the stall faster because buyers prefer costlier herbs.
Nearby competing stalls remove all price constraints because each seller sets prices independently.
Rising Saturday demand forces the stallholder to cut prices to attract more visitors.

title: The Law of Demand
statements: The demand curve slopes downward because marginal buyers drop out as price increases.
Ceteris paribus means other demand shifters such as income are held constant when price changes.
Higher concert ticket prices increase quantity demanded because buyers treat tickets as prestige goods.
Lower coat prices reduce quantity demanded because buyers expect inferior quality.
The law of demand states that quantity demanded rises whenever price rises.

title: Demand Schedules and Curves
statements: Quantity demanded refers to a specific amount at a specific price, not the entire curve.
Plotting a demand schedule yields an upward-sloping curve matching the law of supply.
A demand schedule lists quantities suppliers would offer at successive prices.
Movement along a demand curve results from a change in consumer income.
Quantity demanded remains fixed at every price because buyers must purchase essentials.

title: Innsbruck Ski Equipment Hire
statements: Heavy snowfall forecasts can shift demand rightward for hire equipment independently of the posted daily rate.
Higher rental rates increase quantity demanded because holiday visitors budget more for equipment.
Competing discounts nearby leave quantity demanded unchanged because customers ignore substitutes.
Charging above equilibrium clears inventory faster because customers prefer scarce rentals.
Peak-season demand shifts always lower equilibrium rental rates to attract tourists.

title: The Law of Supply
statements: The law of supply states that, other things equal, quantity supplied rises when price rises.
The supply curve slopes upward because buyers demand more whenever sellers cut output.
At low prices producers supply maximum output to recover fixed costs quickly.
Movement along a supply curve reflects a change in technology holding price fixed.
Higher wheat prices reduce quantity supplied because farming costs rise with crop value.
context: Analyze the direct relationship between a good's price and the quantity producers are willing to offer. Evaluate the following economic assertions:

title: Supply Schedules and Curves
statements: Plotting a supply schedule yields an upward-sloping curve in price–quantity space.
Quantity supplied and supply are identical terms for the entire curve.
Producers supply less at higher prices because profit margins shrink on every unit.
A supply schedule lists quantities buyers would purchase at successive prices.
A price increase shifts the entire supply curve leftward without changing quantity supplied.

title: Graz Bakery Morning Rush
statements: When supply and demand intersect, the bakery neither systematically runs out nor piles up unsold rolls.
Early office meetings shift supply rightward because bakeries open earlier without demand changing.
A flour price spike shifts demand rightward because customers seek cheaper carbohydrates.
Pricing above equilibrium sells out faster because customers interpret higher price as higher quality.
Higher bread prices reduce morning output because expensive flour discourages baking.

title: Market Equilibrium
statements: Graphically, equilibrium occurs where the demand and supply curves intersect.
Equilibrium price is where quantity demanded equals quantity supplied in a market.
At equilibrium, there is no tendency for price to change from ongoing pressure of surplus or shortage.
Markets tend toward equilibrium as price adjustments reduce surplus or shortage.
The equilibrium quantity is the amount actually traded when supply matches demand.
context: Analyze the price and quantity at which quantity demanded equals quantity supplied. Evaluate the following economic assertions:

title: Adjusting Toward Equilibrium
statements: If price is below equilibrium, quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied, creating shortage.
A shortage at the current price puts upward pressure on price as buyers compete for limited goods.
A surplus at the current price puts downward pressure on price as sellers compete to attract buyers.
If price is above equilibrium, quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded, creating surplus.
Competitive markets use price changes to coordinate plans when quantities demanded and supplied diverge.
context: Review how surpluses and shortages prompt price changes that move markets toward equilibrium. Evaluate the following economic assertions:

title: Linz Rental Housing Listings
statements: At equilibrium rent, the number of vacant units neither grows nor shrinks persistently across weeks.
New apartment construction shifting supply rightward can lower equilibrium rent if demand stays fixed.
Cutting asking rent reduces quantity demanded because tenants prefer costlier apartments.
Vacant flats persisting for weeks prove asking rent is below equilibrium because tenants avoid cheap flats.
Heavy tenant competition always lowers equilibrium rent because landlords fear regulation.

title: Surplus in Product Markets
statements: A surplus exists when quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded at the prevailing price.
Surplus puts downward pressure on price because sellers compete to reduce excess stock.
Price above equilibrium is consistent with shortage because buyers crave expensive goods.
Rapid sell-outs and empty shelves typically signal a surplus at the current price.
A harvest bumper crop eliminates surplus because larger supply always matches demand exactly.
context: Analyze conditions where quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded at a given price. Evaluate the following economic assertions:

title: Shortage in Product Markets
statements: Long queues and rapid sell-outs often signal a shortage at the posted price.
A price ceiling set below equilibrium can create persistent shortage in a competitive market.
At a price below equilibrium, quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied until price adjusts.
Shortage puts upward pressure on price as buyers compete for limited available units.
A shortage exists when quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded at the prevailing price.
context: Review conditions where quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied at a given price. Evaluate the following economic assertions:

title: Salzburg Festival Ticket Queue
statements: Minutes-long sell-outs at the posted price suggest quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied.
Overnight queues form when buyers expect shortage at the official price.
Persistent shortage forces resellers to cut prices below the sold-out official rate.
Adding extra performances shifts demand leftward because audiences dislike additional shows.
Raising the official ticket price increases shortage because fewer buyers withdraw.

title: Income as a Demand Shifter
statements: Income changes shift the entire demand curve rather than moving along it.
For inferior goods, rising income can shift demand leftward as buyers switch to higher-quality substitutes.
A recession reducing household income shifts demand rightward for discretionary electronics.
Higher consumer income shifts demand leftward for normal goods because buyers save everything.
A pay rise for office workers lowers equilibrium coffee price because richer buyers demand discounts.

title: Tastes and Preferences
statements: Advertising that increases brand preference shifts demand rightward for the advertised good.
Seasonal fashion trends shifting tastes can change equilibrium clothing prices within a year.
A health trend favouring oat milk can shift demand rightward for oat beverages at each price.
When substitutes become fashionable, demand for the original good may shift leftward.
Negative publicity about a product shifts supply leftward because producers feel discouraged.

title: Styrian Wine Tasting Boom
statements: Surging visitor demand with limited tour slots can create shortage at the posted tasting price.
Award publicity can shift demand rightward for regional wine tastings at unchanged ticket prices.
Higher equilibrium tasting fees may result if demand shifts right while supply remains constrained.
Raising tasting fees can reduce shortage by lowering quantity demanded along the demand curve.
Expanded visiting hours shift demand leftward because tourists dislike longer schedules.

title: Prices of Substitute Goods
statements: Firms monitor substitute pricing because cross-price shifts alter their equilibrium sales.
Substitute price changes shift demand rather than causing movement along the demand curve.
Cheaper streaming subscriptions may shift demand leftward for cinema tickets.
Coffee shops see lower demand when nearby tea prices increase because beverages are complements.
A rise in petrol prices shifts demand leftward for public transport because travel becomes undesirable.

title: Prices of Complementary Goods
statements: A rise in game console prices may shift demand leftward for compatible game titles.
When complements become costlier, equilibrium quantity of the paired good may fall.
Reduced air fares can shift demand rightward for airport parking and hotel rooms near terminals.
Lower printer prices can shift demand rightward for ink cartridges.
Complementary price changes shift demand for the related good, not supply directly.

title: Electric Bus Fleet Procurement
statements: Higher diesel costs can shift demand rightward for electric buses as substitutes become costlier.
A subsidy lowering effective purchase price shifts demand rightward for electric buses.
Expanded battery production shifting supply rightward can reduce equilibrium electric bus prices.
If electric bus prices stay fixed while demand shifts right, surplus appears at current contract offers.
At equilibrium contract price, manufacturers deliver buses cities refuse to operate.

title: Input Costs and Supply
statements: When energy costs surge, equilibrium price may rise if demand remains unchanged.
Higher wages paid to warehouse staff can shift supply leftward for distribution services.
Cheaper imported components can shift supply rightward and lower equilibrium price.
Input cost changes move producers along the supply curve without shifting it.
A drop in steel prices shifts demand leftward because buyers expect weaker furniture.

title: Technology and Productivity
statements: Technological progress that cuts unit cost shifts supply rightward, not leftward.
Improved irrigation technology may shift supply rightward for orchard fruit at each market price.
Automated sorting equipment can shift supply rightward for parcel delivery services.
Technology changes are supply shifters distinct from movements caused by the good's own price.
Rightward supply shifts from technology raise equilibrium price when demand is unchanged.

title: Plant Capacity Expansion
statements: If demand stays fixed while supply shifts right, equilibrium price may fall.
At the new equilibrium, quantity traded may exceed the old equilibrium if demand is unchanged.
Higher raw-material input prices could partially offset the expansion by shifting supply leftward.
Customers ordering the product face lower shortage risk after a successful supply expansion.
Adding capacity that lowers unit cost can shift supply rightward for the manufactured good.

title: Number of Sellers in a Market
statements: New bakeries opening on the same street shift supply rightward for local bread.
Exit of several suppliers during a crisis can create shortage at previously stable prices.
Entry of low-cost online retailers can lower equilibrium prices for standardised goods.
Farmers exiting a crop after poor seasons shift supply leftward for that harvest.
Market supply equals the largest individual seller's supply ignoring smaller rivals.

title: Producer Expectations and Supply
statements: If producers expect costs to fall next month, some may delay production, shifting current supply leftward.
Expected future shortages motivate producers to halt current output entirely.
Expectations of higher future wheat prices increase current supply as farmers dump inventory.
Expectations about future conditions move producers along today's supply curve only.
Storage decisions based on future price outlook leave current market supply unchanged.

title: Harvest Season Labour Contracts
statements: Expectations of a large harvest can shift supply rightward for contract picker labour in August.
Timely contract signing before peak harvest can reduce later shortage when sugar levels spike.
If offered wages sit below equilibrium, vineyards may face shortage of available pickers.
Competing fruit regions raising wages may shift supply leftward for pickers in Styria.
Higher offered day rates typically increase the quantity of pickers willing to supply labour.

title: Simultaneous Demand and Supply Shifts
statements: The net effect on equilibrium price depends on the relative size of demand and supply shifts.
Graphical analysis compares new intersection points to identify changed equilibrium outcomes.
If demand shifts right while supply shifts left, equilibrium price is likely to rise.
If demand shifts right and supply shifts right together, equilibrium quantity rises.
Supply and demand shifts can occur together after a natural disaster disrupts production and tastes.

title: Price Ceilings Below Equilibrium
statements: Non-price rationing such as queues may appear when ceilings create persistent shortage.
A ceiling set above equilibrium is not binding because market price stays below the cap.
Rent controls set below market equilibrium can leave landlords with fewer units to lease.
At the ceiling price, quantity supplied typically exceeds quantity demanded.
A price ceiling below equilibrium prevents price from falling to eliminate surplus.

title: Graz Rent-Control Apartment Search
statements: Long waiting lists for controlled units signal excess demand at the regulated rent.
Controlled rents below open-market levels can create persistent shortage of available flats.
Landlords may redirect maintenance spending when regulated rents cover rising costs poorly.

title: Price Floors Above Equilibrium
statements: A price floor above equilibrium prevents price from falling to eliminate surplus.
Government purchase programs sometimes accompany agricultural price floors to absorb surplus.
At the floor price, quantity supplied typically exceeds quantity demanded.
A floor set below equilibrium is not binding because market price stays above the minimum.
Minimum prices intended to help sellers eliminate all unsold stock immediately.

title: Minimum Wage in Labour Markets
statements: Labour markets use wages as prices coordinating workers' supply and employers' demand.
Employers reduce quantity demanded of labour when mandatory wages rise above equilibrium.
A minimum wage set below equilibrium is not binding for market outcomes.
A minimum wage above the market-clearing wage eliminates all unemployment immediately.
At a binding minimum wage, every worker willing to work finds employment instantly.

title: Alpine Dairy Milk Quota Meeting
statements: Higher feed costs can shift supply leftward for raw milk at each farmgate price.
Cutting quota levels after a glut can help move the market toward equilibrium by reducing surplus.
If farmgate price stays fixed while feed costs rise, farmers expand output to celebrate.
A cooperative quota limiting deliveries increases quantity supplied by forcing extra production.
Surging milk output without matching demand creates shortage at the old farmgate price.

title: Inflation as Rising Price Levels
statements: Inflation is measured using price indices that track many goods and services together.
Central banks often monitor inflation when setting policies that influence interest rates.
Households purchasing the same basket notice inflation when that basket costs more over time.
Moderate inflation reduces the real purchasing power of money held without interest.
Inflation describes a one-day sale discount on a single retail product.

title: Too Much Money Chasing Goods
statements: Inflation from monetary expansion differs from a single crop failure raising one food price.
If everyone spends newly printed money quickly, aggregate demand can rise faster than supply.
Inflation may accelerate when money supply growth outpaces growth in real output.
Holding other factors fixed, larger money supply reduces spending pressure on limited goods.
Too much money chasing too few goods explains deflation in monetary economics.

title: Central Bank Note-Issuance Debate
statements: Shopkeepers reporting broadly rising supplier invoices suggest upward pressure on the price level.
Inflation erodes the real value of cash savings when prices rise faster than interest earned.
Funding repairs through new money may increase spending before additional goods and services appear.
Rapid note issuance without matching output growth can contribute to inflationary pressure.
Policymakers weighing note issuance must consider whether output can absorb extra spending.

title: Interest Rates and Inflation Control
statements: Higher interest rates can reduce borrowing and spending, easing inflationary demand pressure.
Higher rates reward saving and can shift spending from today to later periods.
Interest rate increases operate partly by making loans for homes and equipment more expensive.
Monetary tightening through higher rates aims to align money growth with sustainable output.
Central banks may raise policy rates when inflation persistently exceeds target.

title: Tightening Monetary Policy
statements: Higher mortgage rates following policy tightening can reduce quantity demanded for new housing loans.
Central banks face a trade-off timing challenge because rate effects appear with lags.
Tightening monetary policy typically involves raising key interest rates or reducing money growth.
Business investment accelerates when higher rates raise the cost of financed equipment purchases.
Policy tightening can never reduce inflation because spending is fixed.
context: Review how central banks tighten policy by raising interest rates to combat inflation. Evaluate the following economic assertions:

title: Vienna Mortgage Rate Shopping
statements: Higher saving returns after rate rises may shift some spending from consumption to deposits.
Postponing a flat purchase reduces current quantity demanded for housing credit.
Central bank rate rises aim to accelerate spending that contributes to inflation.
If many households delay purchases, equilibrium home prices rise because fewer buyers compete.
Higher mortgage reference rates reduce monthly borrowing costs for a given loan amount.

title: Demand Increase at Equilibrium
statements: Graphically, a demand shift right moves equilibrium up along an upward-sloping supply curve.
Producers respond to higher equilibrium price by reducing quantity supplied along the supply curve.
More buyers entering a market moves buyers along the demand curve without shifting it.
A rightward demand shift with unchanged supply lowers both equilibrium price and quantity.
After demand increases, quantity demanded stays below quantity supplied permanently.

title: Supply Decrease at Equilibrium
statements: At the new equilibrium after supply falls, quantity demanded equals the reduced quantity supplied.
Buyers facing higher prices reduce quantity demanded along the demand curve after supply falls.
A leftward supply shift with unchanged demand typically raises equilibrium price and lowers quantity.
Production disruptions can shift supply leftward even when buyer preferences stay constant.
Graphically, a supply shift left moves equilibrium up along a downward-sloping demand curve.

title: Population Growth and Market Demand
statements: Markets adjust through price when population growth increases quantity demanded at old prices.
Population growth in a city can shift demand rightward for public transport services.
Immigration increasing local consumers can raise equilibrium apartment rents if housing supply is slow.
Demographic changes move buyers along the demand curve without shifting it.
A shrinking town population shifts demand rightward because remaining residents spend more.

title: Taxes on Producers and Supply
statements: A per-unit tax on producers raises effective production cost and can shift supply leftward.
The statutory incidence on producers can reduce market quantity below the prior equilibrium.
After a producer tax, sellers require lower prices to supply the same quantity as before.
Equilibrium price paid by buyers falls when producer taxes reduce quantity supplied.
Producer taxes move sellers along the supply curve without shifting it.

title: Subsidies to Producers and Supply
statements: Subsidised farmers may supply more output at each market price after receiving per-unit payments.
Rightward supply shifts from subsidies raise equilibrium price if demand stays unchanged.
Subsidies differ from price ceilings because both cap buyer prices identically.
Taxpayer-funded subsidies reduce quantity supplied at each price by confusing producers.
Production subsidies lowering effective costs shift demand leftward for the subsidised good.

title: Weather Shocks and Agricultural Supply
statements: Drought reducing crop yields shifts supply leftward for affected harvests at each price.
Importers may partially offset domestic supply shifts by increasing quantity supplied from abroad.
Short-run food markets may show sharp price spikes after sudden supply leftward shifts.
Frost damaging orchards can raise equilibrium fruit prices if demand remains largely unchanged.
Weather shocks are demand-side events identical to changes in consumer tastes.

title: Consumer Expectations and Demand
statements: If buyers expect prices to fall next month, current quantity demanded may decrease today.
Expectations of higher future petrol prices can shift current demand rightward as drivers stock up.
Expected future income growth may shift current demand rightward for durable goods like appliances.
Expectations about future conditions move buyers along the demand curve only.
Panic buying before announced rationing reflects a leftward demand shift at unchanged official prices.
context: Analyze how expectations about future prices or income shift current demand. Evaluate the following economic assertions:

title: Labour Market Wage Adjustment
statements: Labour market equilibrium occurs where quantity supplied of labour equals quantity demanded.
Competition among employers for scarce workers can bid wages up toward labour market equilibrium.
Higher wages typically reduce quantity supplied of labour as workers reject paid work.
Skill shortages in tech hiring resemble goods surpluses with downward wage pressure.
Employers hire more workers when wages rise above the value of marginal output at the margin.
context: Review how wages coordinate quantity supplied and demanded of labour like prices in goods markets. Evaluate the following economic assertions:

title: Global Supply Chain Disruption
statements: Domestic equilibrium price may rise when import supply falls while demand stays constant.
Global markets isolate domestic equilibrium from supply shocks abroad completely.
Firms may seek alternate suppliers over time, shifting demand leftward permanently.
Port closures delaying imports shift demand rightward for components used in domestic assembly.
Shortages of imported parts increase quantity supplied of finished goods domestically.
context: Analyze how international supply disruptions shift domestic market supply. Evaluate the following economic assertions:

title: Integrated Market Mechanisms Review
statements: Understanding markets requires separating movement along curves from shifts caused by other factors.
Inflation linked to excessive money growth may be addressed by tighter policy raising interest rates.
Price ceilings below equilibrium create shortage; price floors above equilibrium create surplus.
Demand shifters include income, tastes, and substitute prices; supply shifters include costs and technology.
Surplus and shortage signals guide competitive markets toward equilibrium through price adjustment.
